title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's corporate policies and operating procedures for: annual budgeting and rolling forecasting; procurement and purchase order workflows; contract lifecycle and legal review standards; and revenue recognition and billing practices. It is intended for budget owners, finance partners, legal, procurement, and product/GTM leaders who own commercial terms and customer billing.

Scope

Applies to: all corporate functions (Engineering, Product, Sales, GTM, Ops, Finance, Legal) and all purchasing or revenue-generating agreements executed by Redwood Inference, across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private product lines.

Goals

- Provide a repeatable, auditable budgeting and forecasting cadence that drives resource allocation decisions.
- Reduce contracting cycle time while ensuring appropriate legal and risk review.
- Centralize procurement approvals and preferred-vendor usage to control costs and compliance.
- Ensure revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606 principles and accounting best practices.

Key contacts

- Finance (general): finance@redwood.ai
- Legal (contracts): legal@redwood.ai
- Procurement & vendor ops: procurement@redwood.ai
- Revenue ops / Billing: billing@redwood.ai

1) Budgeting and Forecasting

Overview and cadence

- Annual Budgeting: led by Finance. Planning kicks off in Q3 and concludes with board-approved operating plan by the end of the fiscal year (calendar year).
- Quarterly Re-forecast: rolling 12-month forecast updated quarterly to reflect actuals, new bookings, and major cost changes.
- Monthly Close Forecast: top-level revenue and spend forecast updated monthly for leadership review.

Timeline (example)

1. August: Budget kickoff, templates distributed to owners.
2. September-October: Department-level submissions and cross-functional alignment.
3. November: Finance consolidates, stress-tests scenarios (base/upsell/downturn).
4. December: Final leadership review and board approval.

Templates and controls

- Use the centralized Budget Workbook (Finance Drive: /budgets/2025/budget-workbook-v1.xlsx).
- Each cost center must provide: headcount plan, SaaS/capital spend requests, revenue assumptions, and KPIs.
- Variance threshold: any budget line with projected variance > 5% and > $25k must include a root-cause analysis and mitigation plan.

Approval flow and ownership

- Budget owners: department leads (Product, Eng, Sales, Ops) own inputs and variance explanations.
- Approvals: Manager -> Director -> Finance business partner -> CFO (final sign-off for departments).
- Exceptions: material changes (>10% of department budget or >$250k) require Executive Committee review.

2) Contracts and Legal Process

Contract lifecycle

- Template-first approach: always start with the approved contract template for the product type (Hosted API Master Services Agreement, Dedicated Services Addendum, Private Deployment License).
- Contract creation: Sales/Account Execs draft using template; upload to Contract Management System (CMS) with key metadata (customer name, contract value, term, renewal, special clauses).
- Legal review: required for any deviation from template or non-standard clause.

Mandatory legal review thresholds

- All NDAs: Legal review required.
- Commercial contracts with total contract value (TCV) >= $100,000: mandatory legal + finance review.
- Any contract including data residency, sub-processing, or unusual IP clauses: legal + security review.

Signature authority

- Sales Manager / Director: can sign customer quotes up to $25k with standard T&Cs.
- VP Sales: up to $250k with Legal concurrence.
- CFO / CEO: > $250k or non-standard terms (CFO routinely signs enterprise MSAs).

Contract retention and tracking

- All executed contracts must be stored in the CMS and linked to Salesforce opportunity. Contracts are retained for a minimum of 7 years.
- Contract metadata must include: contract owner, value, term, renewal notice period, and customer billing cadence.

Contract review checklist (example)

1. Parties and effective dates - verified.
2. Scope of services and SLAs - include product name and endpoints.
3. Fees & payment terms - billing cadence, late fees.
4. Data processing and confidentiality - DPA required for customer data.
5. Liability caps and indemnities - align to policy.
6. Termination & transition assistance - ensure data return provisions.
7. Signature authority confirmed.

3) Procurement Procedures

Purchase request and approval matrix

- Purchase request (PR) must be created in the Procurement System for all purchases > $1,000.
- Approval thresholds:
  - <= $5,000: direct manager approval.
  - $5,001 - $50,000: Director + Finance business partner.
  - $50,001 - $250,000: VP + Procurement + Finance.
  - > $250,000: CFO approval and competitive procurement process (see RFP section).

Vendor selection and preferred vendors

- Use preferred-vendor list when available (Procurement will maintain list, updated quarterly). Preferred vendors have negotiated rates, master agreements, and established SSO/PO processes.
- For strategic or high-value spend (> $50k), Procurement will run an RFP with at least 3 qualified vendors and produce an evaluation scorecard.

Purchase order and invoice matching

- Procurement issues a PO prior to supplier work when spend exceeds $5k.
- Finance performs a three-way match (PO, goods/services receipt, invoice) for all PO-based purchases. Discrepancies > $500 must be escalated to Procurement.

Capital vs Operating spend

- Capital purchases (hardware, multi-year licenses meeting capitalization thresholds) must be pre-cleared with Finance; capital requests go through the CapEx approval workflow.

Exceptions and emergency purchases

- Emergency procurement (production incident remediation) may bypass standard RFP if authorized by an on-call director and logged in the Procurement System within 24 hours. Post-facto review required.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies

Accounting standard and high-level approach

- Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606 (IFRS 15 equivalent): 1) identify contract(s) with customer, 2) identify performance obligations, 3) determine transaction price, 4) allocate price to obligations, 5) recognize revenue when obligations are satisfied.

Product-specific guidance

- Hosted API (usage-based): revenue recognized as usage occurs (per invoice period). Usage measured and validated by backend metering; invoiced monthly in arrears unless customer contract states otherwise.
- Dedicated (committed capacity): if customer prepays for a term, revenue is deferred and recognized ratably over the committed term unless there are separate performance obligations (e.g., professional services).
- Private Deployment (license + services): split invoicing where license may be recognized on delivery/transfer of license if criteria are met; services (installation, customization, support) recognized over time as delivered.

Billing cadence and invoice rules

- Standard hosted customers: monthly invoicing in arrears; payment terms NET 30.
- Dedicated reserved capacity: invoiced per contract (monthly in arrears or upfront per contract).
- Professional services: milestone-based invoicing tied to SOW deliverables.
- All invoices must reference the Sales Order number and the CMS contract ID.

Deferred revenue and contract liability accounting

- Payments received in advance are recorded to Contract Liabilities (deferred revenue). Revenue is recognized from deferred revenue monthly according to the recognition schedule in the general ledger.
- Finance reconciles deferred revenue balances monthly and provides roll-forward schedules for audit.

Credits, refunds, and dispute handling

- Credit policy: credits for billing disputes are limited to validated meter or contractual errors. Credits/refunds require Finance approval and a linked dispute ticket in Zendesk/Salesforce.
- Billing disputes must be raised within 60 days of invoice issuance to be considered for credit. Older disputes require CFO approval.

Revenue thresholds and reporting

- Any single contract with TCV > $500k must be reviewed by Revenue Operations and Accounting to confirm allocation and timing of recognition (opinion documented).
- Monthly revenue close: Revenue Ops provides usage reports by product line by the 5th business day; Finance posts recognized revenue by the 10th business day.

Operational controls and auditability

- Metering & billing audits: internal controls around usage metering (logs, reconciliation) to ensure billable units are accurate. Significant meter changes must be change-controlled.
- Segregation of duties: Billing generation, invoice approval, and cash application functions are separated across teams.

Appendices and templates

- Contract templates: Hosted-API-MSA-template.docx; Dedicated-Services-Addendum.docx; DPA-template.docx. (Stored in CMS /templates).
- Procurement forms: PR-form-v2.pdf, RFP-evaluation-scorecard.xlsx (Procurement Drive).
- Budget template: budget-workbook-v1.xlsx (Finance Drive).
- Revenue recognition checklist: revrec-checklist.xlsx (Accounting Drive).

Change history and policy governance

- Policy owner: Head of Finance (Aisha Patel).
- Review cadence: Annual review (or sooner for regulatory changes).
- Change log: key updates must be recorded in the CMS and stakeholders notified via email and Slack #finance-announce.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ)

- Q: Who do I contact for contract exceptions?
  A: legal@redwood.ai with contract metadata and proposed clause.
- Q: What if a vendor refuses our PO terms?
  A: Escalate to Procurement; do not accept invoice-based terms >$50k without Procurement approval.
